Row.Text: Re-dealable Leader Abilities, Attributes, and Start Biases

Shuffles leader abilities, attributes and start terrain at the start of a game. Leaders can swap abilities, swap everything, or have the separate bonuses inside each ability mixed between them, and you can turn abilities, attributes or start terrain off for everyone. It works in multiplayer through the game's own lobby, and the game's leader screens show what each leader ended up with, including where they like to start.
Only the host can change these settings. You'll see them update here as the host changes them.
Pick a civilization on the civilization select screen first; a Random civilization can't be built.
Fill your civilization's slots from the cards below: an ability, its uniques and its start terrain, from any civilization of this age.

No start terrain of their own: they start where their civilization likes to.
Your leader starts near {1_Terrain}, the way a leader with that start terrain of their own would.
Taking a civilization's ability gives that civilization yours in return. A unique moves, and its civilization goes without it.
Each AI player can be built the way you build your own leader and civilization. Up to {1_Total} AI leaders can be built in one game; the rest are shuffled.
No AI players in this game.
Random leader: give this slot a leader in the player rows to build it.
No civilization picked for this slot yet.
Fill your leader's slots from the cards below. Whatever you don't take is shuffled among the AI leaders.
Pick a leader on the leader select screen first; a Random slot can't be built.
The preset is Base game, so these picks won't be used. Pick a preset above to build.
Only the host builds a leader in this version.

This bonus can't be taken on its own yet.
AI players and Random slots only get civilizations ticked in this pool. A civilization a player picks by hand stays as picked. For now this only applies to the first age.
No leaders in this pool yet. A slot set to Random from this pool gets a normal random leader.
None of the leader mods this mod supports are installed and turned on, so leaders from other mods play normally.

Sets the six rows below at once. Base game: nothing moves. Full random: leader abilities swap whole, attributes split up, start terrain is a random roll. Paired random: attributes and start terrain follow the ability. Logical split random: abilities and attributes split up, start terrain is logical with the bonuses. Split random: the same, start terrain a random roll. Change a row by hand and this reads Custom.
The terrain each leader prefers to start near (the game calls it a start bias). Off entirely: the map places everyone without any terrain preference.
Where each leader's ability goes. Off entirely: no leader has an ability this game.
Where each leader's attributes go. Off entirely: no leader starts with attributes, and everyone gets all twelve diplomatic actions instead, so it's even.
Human players keep their own leader
Each human player plays their chosen leader exactly as normal. Only the AI leaders are shuffled, among themselves.

Unticked leaders play exactly as normal. Only leaders in this game are shuffled with each other, Random slots included. In an online game, if another human leaves their slot on Random, every ticked leader joins the shuffle, so a bonus can come from a leader who isn't playing.
Lets abilities of supported leaders from other mods into the shuffle. The leader's mod has to be installed, turned on, and pass a check when the game is set up. Other modded leaders play normally.
Lets attributes of supported leaders from other mods into the shuffle. The leader's mod has to be installed, turned on, and pass a check when the game is set up. Other modded leaders play normally.

Lets start terrain of supported leaders from other mods into the shuffle. The leader's mod has to be installed, turned on, and pass a check when the game is set up. Other modded leaders play normally.
The supported modded leaders you have installed. Unticked ones play exactly as their mod made them.
Tick leaders for the pool. A player slot set to Random from the pool gets one of them when the game starts; a slot on plain Random can still get any leader.
Whose agendas and favorite civilizations an AI leader plays by after the shuffle.
Only matters on a row set to Split up: whether each leader or civilization gets a fair share of the strong bonuses.
When you can see what the other leaders ended up with.
The same number with the same settings and leaders gives the same shuffle, so a friend can play the same one. A new number is picked each time you set up a game, and it shows on the loading screen.
Nothing moves: every leader and civilization plays as shipped. A row set to Off entirely still applies.
Leader abilities swap whole, attributes split up, start terrain is a random roll. None of the three is tied to the others.

Leader abilities swap whole, and the attributes and start terrain follow the ability, so each leader gets another leader's whole package. Amina might play with Pachacuti's mountain bonuses and start beside mountains.

Leader abilities and attributes split up: every bonus and attribute is dealt out to a random leader, each giving as many as it gets. Start terrain fits the bonuses, so whoever ends up with mountain bonuses starts near mountains.
The same deal as Logical split random, with start terrain a random roll instead.
The rows below were set by hand.
Each leader keeps its own ability.
Each leader gets another leader's whole ability.
Abilities are broken into their separate bonuses and dealt out to random leaders; each leader gets back as many as it gave.
Each leader keeps its own attributes.
Attributes are dealt out one by one to random leaders; each leader gets back as many as it gave.
The attributes go wherever the ability went: a leader takes the attributes of the leader whose ability it got (with split bonuses, the leader it got the most from).
Each leader and civilization keeps its own start terrain.
Start terrain that is logical with the bonuses the leader now holds, so whoever has mountain bonuses starts near mountains; civilizations swap start terrain within their age.
The start terrain goes wherever the ability went; civilizations swap start terrain within their age.
Start terrain is picked at random for every leader and civilization, from nobody in particular.
Where each civilization's ability goes, always within its own age. Off entirely: no civilization has an ability this game.
Where a civilization's unique units and improvements go (its unique buildings and quarters go with its civics). Off entirely: no civilization can build its uniques this game.
Each civilization keeps its own ability.
Civilization abilities are broken into their separate bonuses and dealt out to random civilizations of the same age; each civilization gets back as many as it gave.
Each civilization gets another civilization's whole ability, from the same age.
Each civilization keeps its own uniques.
The uniques go wherever the civilization's ability went: whoever has Rome's ability also has the Legion.
Each civilization gets another same-age civilization's whole set of uniques, apart from the abilities.
Where a civilization's unique civics go: its civics tree, its traditions, and the unique buildings, quarters and units those civics unlock. Off entirely: no civilization has unique civics this game.
Each civilization keeps its own civics.
The civics go wherever the civilization's ability went.
Each civilization gets another same-age civilization's civics, apart from the abilities.
Moves between leaders as the preset says.
Taken out of the game for everyone, so it's even. A leader or civilization you built by hand keeps what you gave it.
An AI leader keeps its own agendas and favorite civilizations, while playing the bonuses it got.
An AI leader plays by the agendas and favorite civilizations of the leader its bonuses came from. With split bonuses, the leader it got the most from.
Agendas and favorite civilizations swap between the AI leaders on their own, unconnected to the bonuses.
Each leader's bonuses add up to about the same strength, so nobody gets all the strong ones.
Bonuses go out at random, so one leader can end up much stronger than another.
The leader screens show what everyone got from the moment you set up the game.
You see your own at setup. Another leader's shows in the diplomacy panel and the Civilopedia after you've met them.
A random leader from the Leader pool, picked when the game starts. If the pool is empty or every leader in it is taken, the slot gets a normal random leader.
Starts anywhere the map puts them
Starts where this map places them; it doesn't use start biases
Leader abilities are off for this game.
You haven't met this leader yet.
